audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents an ability: it refers five times to Lillia's 'W Watchful Wisp dash' and tells you to walk her down 'when her W dash is on cooldown'. Lillia's W is Watch Out! Eep!, and it is not a dash — Lillia has no dash anywhere in her kit. It also calls Blooming Blows an auto-reset, which it is not.
audit.why: Riot's text for W: 'Lillia deals damage in a nearby area, dealing heavy damage in the center' — 500 range, 14/13/12/11/10, zone damage only. Blooming Blows passively grants stacking move speed on spell hits and actively damages nearby enemies with extra true damage on the edge; nothing about it resets an attack. Her only escape is the move speed she accumulates, which is why denying her spell hits is what kills the kite.
audit.corrected: Every 'W dash' reference removed and replaced with the real behaviour: no dash, move-speed stacking, and Zaahen's E (10s) plus 850-range W pull as the tools that outreach her 450 Q and 500 W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed with the whys beside them — rows 2, 3, 5 and 6 read Skill while their whys said 'tilts to you', 'favor you', 'out-scale her' and 'you crush her'; row 4 read Zaahen while its why called it a skill-check.
audit.why: The packet levelChart and the audited mirror agree: Skill, Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen, Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen.
audit.corrected: All five rows proposed as matched full+content pairs with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lilting Lullaby was described as a delayed sleep with no cooldown, no range, and no precondition.
audit.why: It is 150/130/110 at 1600 range and only affects enemies already carrying Dream Dust from a prior spell hit. If she has not landed anything on you it does nothing — which turns 'avoid her ult' into the concrete rule 'avoid her spell hits'. Waking a sleeping target deals extra damage, so it punishes a dive rather than only setting one up.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the 150s figure, the Dream Dust precondition and the wake-up damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that armour is the wrong stat against her.
audit.why: Blooming Blows deals extra true damage on its edge and her passive deals max-health damage over time — the flagged resistances-invalidated case.

edits.before: This is where you take over. Lillia is a squishy, mobility-reliant skirmisher who wants to kite with Q Blooming Blows auto-resets, but your Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught let you close the gap and burst her before her passive Dream Dust ramps. Walk her down when her W Watchful Wisp dash is on cooldown and you win the trade outright.
edits.after: This is where you take over. Lillia is a squishy skirmisher with no dash — she kites on the stacking move speed from Blooming Blows (Q), so denying her spell hits is what strands her. Your E closes on 10s and your W pulls from 850, more than her 450 Q or 500 W can answer. Walk her down and the trade is yours outright.

edits.before: Her R Lullaby is the equalizer — the delayed sleep can set up a jungle gank or peel your engage. Cleanse the drowsy by pre-committing E onto her before the sleep lands, and don't dive under tower into a Lullaby without your R Final Retribution ready to finish before she wakes you into a counter.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby is the equalizer at 150s and 1600 range, but it only touches targets already carrying Dream Dust — if she has not landed a spell on you first, the ultimate does nothing at all. Waking a sleeping target deals bonus damage, so never dive under tower while it is up without your R banked to finish.

edits.before: You out-scale her early item timing as a Juggernaut: your durability plus Q sustain shrugs off her Blooming Blows chip, while she needs many stacks to threaten you. Force short all-ins the moment her W is down and you convert kills.
edits.after: You out-scale her early item timing: your durability plus the heal on your Q shrugs off her chip. Her Q's edge deals true damage though, so armour does not answer it — health and your own healing do. Force short all-ins while her W (14s) is down.

edits.before: Close with Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught while her W dash is down
edits.after: Close with your E dash and the 850 W pull — she has no dash to answer

edits.before: Kite with Q auto-resets and W Watchful Wisp to stay out of your range
edits.after: Kite on Blooming Blows move-speed stacks to stay out of your range

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are your window: you have the tools to close on a mobility-reliant squishy, and your Q plus E combo out-trades her Blooming Blows the moment her W Watchful Wisp is on cooldown. This edge carries into level 6 as a skill-check because her R Lullaby can flip a bad engage, so track her dash and respect the sleep setup.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are your window: she has no dash at all, so your E and your 850-range W pull close on her whenever she has spent Watch Out! Eep! (14s at rank 1). That edge carries into level 6 as a skill-check — Lilting Lullaby only lands on a target already carrying Dream Dust, so respect the spell that sets it up.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kite + move speed stacks. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Blooming Blows: 6s at rank 1, and its edge lands true damage — armour is not the answer. - Swirlseed: a flat 12s, 700 range, rolls on until it hits a wall. - Lilting Lullaby: 150s, and only lands if Dream Dust is on you.

edits.before: Her kite + move speed stacks. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Every spell she lands stacks her move speed — deny the hit, kill the kite.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: She has no dash: your E is for closing on her, not for escaping.
